hook.from: Geography > Location, Terrain, Natural resources; Economy > Exports
hook.excerpt: Southern Asia, between China and India || mostly mountainous with some fertile valleys and savanna || landlocked; strategic location between China and India; controls several key Himalayan mountain passes || Resources: timber, hydropower, gypsum, calcium carbonate || Exports: iron alloys, aircraft, dolomite, semi-finished iron, cement (2023)

physicalGeography.excerpt: mostly mountainous with some fertile valleys and savanna || Southern Asia, between China and India

climate.excerpt: varies; tropical in southern plains; cool winters and hot summers in central valleys; severe winters and cool summers in Himalayas || violent storms from the Himalayas are the source of the country's Bhutanese name, which translates as Land of the Thunder Dragon; frequent landslides during the rainy season

economy.excerpt: hydropower investments spurring economic development; Gross National Happiness economy; sharp poverty declines; low inflation; strong monetary and fiscal policies; stable currency; fairly resilient response to COVID-19; key economic and strategic relations with India; climate vulnerabilities || Exports: iron alloys, aircraft, dolomite, semi-finished iron, cement (2023) || Industries: cement, wood products, processed fruits, alcoholic beverages, calcium carbide, tourism

peopleAndCulture.from: People and Society > Languages, Religions, Ethnic groups, Urbanization
peopleAndCulture.excerpt: Sharchopkha 28%, Dzongkha (official) 24%, Lhotshamkha 22%, other 26% (includes foreign languages) (2005 est.) || Lamaistic Buddhist 75.3%, Indian- and Nepali-influenced Hinduism 22.1%, other 2.6% (2005 est.) || Ngalop (also known as Bhote) 50%, ethnic Nepali 35% (predominantly Lhotshampas), indigenous or migrant tribes 15%
